doc.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000

chapter: Jazz parties, Metropole and San Diego
title: Admission, pay and Sol Yaged at the Metropole
summary: Details of the cheap entry and bandstand, with Cozy Cole and Sol Yaged remembered.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Did they charge to get into this place?
That’s amazing. How did they pay the musicians?

You’d go in and buy a beer. I’m not sure. They had a second story. They may have had an entrance fee because they put the bands up there. It may have cost you fifty cents or a dollar to get in. But you’d go there, and I’d just sit there and drink three or four bottles of beer in the night. Terrific. Marvelous. And as I say you stay at the bar and then as these people came off they’d swing by the bar and say hello and so on and so forth. And I’m trying to think — Cozy Cole. Cozy was there. And just everybody who was anybody in jazz played in that place. All night long. They started in the afternoon and went all night long. And you talk to any of those guys they were all there, and they all played. Well you interviewed Sol Yaged. © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-
He was about the least talented fella there. Nice guy. And he was so proud of the fact that he taught Steve Allen how to play the clarinet for “The Benny Goodman Story.”
And oh there was another clarinet player, Dixie style. Oh you’d know his name too.
It wasn’t that fella that ended up with Armstrong was it?
No, no, no, no. But oh dear — well you’ve got some of his records in the collection.
